answer: A stake-weighted reputation system makes fake identities expensive: each agent must lock a deposit that grows with the volume it wants to move, and that deposit is slashed when peers flag bad work. One honest history becomes a strong signal no fresh clone can copy, because building it takes real time and cost. Like a dune that only shifts grain by grain, the nebula of many cheap identities cannot outrun one verified track record — attackers must pay for every identity they burn.
